source: Grave + death record — James (the brother with a confirmed grave)

grave.cemetery: Glenwood Cemetery, Champlain, Clinton County, NY (Lot B-43, Frederick A. Hubbell family)
grave.marker: Four-brothers Civil War memorial erected by the Sabbath School of the First Presbyterian Church of Champlain
grave.verbatim_inscription_east_face: James HUBBELL / of Co. I. 153 Reg. N.Y.V. / Died at Albany Oct. 12, 1865, while in the Service of his country / AE. 27 Yrs.
grave.source_retrieved: NNY Tombstone Transcription Project (free): https://nnytombstoneproject.nygenweb.net/clinton/champlain/glenwood.html — confirms the memorial verbatim (the same transcription as internal source G11).
grave.note: The memorial is partly a CENOTAPH for the four brothers: Henry's body was never recovered; Alexander is buried in Iowa; Charles likely in Iowa. James — who died at Albany — is the brother most likely actually interred here.

cross_sibling_corroboration.alexander: same memorial: 'Alexander B. HUBBELL ... Died Dec. 7, 1894' — a SECOND independent witness for DSC-2026-06-06-002 (confirms 1894 over 1899).
cross_sibling_corroboration.charles: same memorial: 'Charles F. HUBBELL ... Died Mar. 21, 1875 / AE. 37 Yrs.' — gives Charles a PRECISE death date (Mar 21 1875) and AE 37 -> b. ~1838, corroborating the roster's ~1837 over the genealogy's 1840 (DSC-2026-06-06-003).
cross_sibling_corroboration.henry: same memorial: 'Henry HUBBELL ... fell at the battle of Antietam Sept. 19, 1862 / AE. 24' — note the stone says Sept 19; Antietam was Sept 17 1862 (minor stone error; Henry's sweep already resolved his death as Sept 17).

death.stone_date: 1865-10-12, at Albany, NY ('while in the service of his country')
death.family_intro_date: 1865-10-19 (DOC-INTRO-1996) — 'died on the way home from Savannah'
death.reconciliation: Per the AG roster James mustered out Oct 2 1865 at Savannah, then died ~10 days later at Albany while traveling home. The Oct 12 stone date is corroborated by an independent transcription; the Oct 19 family date is uncorroborated and equals the Cedar Creek wounding date (Oct 19 1864) — likely a conflation. Documentary weight favors OCT 12, 1865 (DSC-2026-06-06-004).
death.place: Albany, NY — likely a U.S. Army general hospital (e.g., Ira Harris U.S. General Hospital, confirmed to operate at Albany 1861-65) or en route. No hospital death register located online (handoff).
death.death_record_handoff: Ancestry coll. 2123 'U.S., Registers of Deaths of Volunteers, 1861-1865' (NARA-derived) — gated; would give cause/place. https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/2123/

findagrave.note: Glenwood Cemetery Champlain exists on FindAGrave (id 64661) but the memorial was not retrievable by automation. Grave is independently confirmed via the NNY transcription, so this is corroboration, not a blocker.

confidence: external · clear · definite (grave); likely (exact death date)
